name: OK-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Frank Lucas running for reelection
Democratic challenger Suzie Byrd has minimal reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Lucas at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: This western Oklahoma seat leans Republican by about 23 points, and veteran incumbent Frank Lucas is running again with a large cash advantage over a little-funded challenger. Markets price Lucas near certain, and no polling or expert ratings suggest anything unusual, so the race stays safely Republican.
model.watch: A surprise wave election or a major scandal involving Lucas would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Frank Lucas, one of the longest-serving members of the Oklahoma delegation, is seeking another term in a district that leans Republican by roughly 23 points. He enters the general election with over half a million dollars on hand, while Democratic nominee Suzie Byrd has reported little or no fundraising activity. No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, which is typical for safely held seats.

Prediction markets give Lucas about a 96 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and his incumbency advantage. The forecast expects Lucas to win by roughly 20 points, with the main uncertainty coming from turnout patterns rather than any competitive dynamic in the race itself.
